turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll explore the repo structure to find streaming-related code.Let me read the fuller relevant sections of these two files directly.I now have a complete picture. Let me confirm the realtime path is a separate (WebSocket) mechanism, not the SSE `core/streaming.ts` path, to note the distinction accurately.Confirmed — Realtime is a separate WebSocket transport (`EventEmitter`-based), independent of the SSE stack. Here's the full picture.

## Core streaming implementation

**`src/core/streaming.ts`** — the foundational primitive, `class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>`.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` — parses a raw `fetch` `Response` as Server-Sent Events (via `_iterSSEMessages`/`SSEDecoder`/`LineDecoder`), yielding parsed JSON items, and throws `APIError` on `data.error`.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used for re-hydrating a stream on another machine/tier, e.g. server → browser).
- Also implements `tee()` and `toReadableStream()` for splitting/re-serializing a stream.

**`src/internal/parse.ts`** (`defaultParseResponse`) — the wiring point: when `props.options.stream` is true, it calls `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client, ...)` (or a custom `options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse` if the request specified one, per `__streamClass?: typeof Stream` in `src/internal/request-options.ts:82`). This is invoked from the client's request pipeline in `src/client.ts`.

Supporting decoders: `src/internal/decoders/line.ts` (`LineDecoder`, `findDoubleNewlineIndex`).

## Higher-level stream helpers (built on `Stream`)

These wrap the raw SSE `Stream<Item>` in an `EventEmitter`-style API with typed events and accumulation/snapshot logic:

- **`src/lib/EventStream.ts`** — base class `EventStream<EventTypes>` (on/off/once/emitted, abort handling).
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`** — `class ChatCompletionStream extends AbstractChatCompletionRunner` (which itself extends `EventStream`). `createChatCompletion()` calls `client.chat.completions.create({...params, stream:true})`, then `_fromReadableStream`/iteration wraps chunks with `Stream.fromReadableStream`, accumulating a `ChatCompletionSnapshot`.
- **`src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts`** — `class ResponseStream extends EventStream`. `ResponseStream.createResponse()` calls `client.responses.create({...params, stream:true})` (or `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})`), iterates the resulting `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` in `_createOrRetrieveResponse`, and accumulates via `src/lib/responses/ResponseAccumulator.ts`.
- **`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`** — `class AssistantStream extends EventStream`, used by the (deprecated) Assistants beta API; also calls `Stream.fromReadableStream`.
- **`src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`** — streaming variant of the tool-calling runner (`runTools` with `stream:true`).

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:73-79` | sets `stream: body.stream ?? false` on the POST → `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(params)` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:221-226` | → `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion(...)` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools(params)` with `stream:true` | `completions.ts:196-216` | → `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools(...)` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-123` | → `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve(id, {stream:true})` | `responses.ts:135-169` | → `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.stream(params)` | `responses.ts:198-206` | → `ResponseStream.createResponse(...)` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy Completions API) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-44` | → `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:75-94` | → `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `images.ts:45-62` | → `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:182-184` | → `AssistantStream.createThreadAssistantStream(...)` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.createAndStream(...)` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` | → `AssistantStream` (found via grep hit; not individually re-read) |

All of the `stream:true` cases above set `stream` on the request options, which `defaultParseResponse` in `src/internal/parse.ts` intercepts to call `Stream.fromSSEResponse`.

## Separate transport: Realtime API (not part of this SSE stack)

`src/realtime/websocket.ts` (`OpenAIRealtimeWebSocket`) and `src/realtime/ws.ts` (`OpenAIRealtimeWS`) both extend `OpenAIRealtimeEmitter` (`src/realtime/internal-base.ts`) — a WebSocket-based, `EventEmitter`-style API unrelated to `core/streaming.ts`. Mentioned for completeness since the README also calls this "streaming," but it doesn't route through `Stream`.

## Not verified
- Exact contents of `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts` `createAndStream` (grep found the method name but I didn't read its body directly — inferred it parallels `createAndRunStream`'s pattern based on `AssistantStream.ts:293` (`_createThreadAssistantStream`) and file naming).
- `src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` internals (only referenced, not read in detail).
- Whether any resource sets `__streamClass` to something other than `Stream` itself — I found the field declared in `request-options.ts` but no call site in the files I sampled; there may be one in files not read (e.g., `resources/beta/chatkit/*`, `resources/videos.ts`).

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/

README:
# OpenAI TypeScript and JavaScript API Library

[![NPM version](<https://img.shields.io/npm/v/openai.svg?label=npm%20(stable)>)](https://npmjs.org/package/openai) ![npm bundle size](https://img.shields.io/bundlephobia/minzip/openai) [![JSR Version](https://jsr.io/badges/@openai/openai)](https://jsr.io/@openai/openai)

This library provides convenient access to the OpenAI REST API from TypeScript or JavaScript.

It is generated from our [OpenAPI specification](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi) with [Stainless](https://stainlessapi.com/).

To learn how to use the OpenAI API, check out our [API Reference](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference) and [Documentation](https://platform.openai.com/docs).

## Installation

```sh
npm install openai
```

### Installation from JSR

```sh
deno add jsr:@openai/openai
npx jsr add @openai/openai
```

These commands will make the module importable from the `@openai/openai` scope. You can also [import directly from JSR](https://jsr.io/docs/using-packages#importing-with-jsr-specifiers) without an install step if you're using the Deno JavaScript runtime:

```ts
import OpenAI from 'jsr:@openai/openai';
```

## Usage

The full API of this library can be found in [api.md file](api.md) along with many [code examples](https://github.com/openai/openai-node/tree/
